spec_anchor: FV-ENGINE-FLOOR-1 (board row) + FV-PBT-FLOOR-BUILD-SPEC.md §2/§3/§4 (pattern reused, not the same denominator) + OCG SPEC.md §21 (properties derived from) + §4 (metamorphic property derived from)
population_definition: one artifact: run_chain, the worker's chain-orchestration engine (mcp-apps-poc/worker.mjs). NOT a member of check-fv-floor-coverage.mjs's kernel population -- see relationship_to_kernel_floor_gate below.
independence_sentence: This item was reviewed and attested independently; the single signature (when applied) is a mechanical convenience over the one enumerated digest, not a bulk review.
per_item_basis_of_review: Oracle-equivalent gate (real fixture-backed chain must complete, produce a 64-hex composite_execution_hash, verify hash_valid===true, and reproduce the identical hash on a second independent run) ran and passed before any property was trusted. All four properties (step order, input threading, gate-table evaluation, metamorphic hash order-independence) ran green. Negative control (--negative-control flag, deliberately flips one passing assertion to failing) run and confirmed to fail as expected -- see negative_control below.
relationship_to_kernel_floor_gate: run_chain is worker-repo orchestration code, not a chaingraph.meta.json kernel -- it has no kernel_digest, no fixtures.json, and is not in check-fv-floor-coverage.mjs's live-kernel denominator. This artifact does not touch that gate, its baseline, or its count in any way. It borrows that rollout's PROVEN zero-dep pattern (mulberry32 PRNG, oracle-then-property pipeline, digest header, PENDING sign-off convention) as a separate, worker-repo-local floor -- not a 579th row.
coverage_boundary: Covers: the integration seam run_chain owns over kernel code it calls -- step ordering (SPEC.md §21.1), parent-hash/chain-depth threading (§21.1, verified via the composite artifact's chain.parent_hashes/parent_tool_ids -- see §21-silence finding #1 for why not the per-step value directly), decision-gate evaluation (§21.4, tested directly against kernels/_gateval.mjs's evaluateGate -- the exact module run_chain imports, not a reimplementation), and that chain position never leaks into a step's own execution_hash (metamorphic, derived from §4's fixed hash preimage). Does NOT cover: cross-runner divergence -- no browser leg exists or is planned (FV-ENGINE-RUNNER-SCOPE-1 found only 2 independent runners exist; CHAIN-DIFF-HARNESS-1, the worker-vs-browser differential, was separately stopped by Tim's 2026-08-10 ruling and is not reopened here). Does NOT cover: individual kernel correctness (each kernel's own floor, if/when it lands, owns that). Does NOT duplicate scripts/run-chain-corpus.mjs (full-corpus completion/determinism/schema-conformance regression, already CI-wired) -- this file is additive on the specific §21.1/§21.4 threading and gate-table obligations that script never asserts.
silence_findings: SPEC.md §21.1 describes per-step chain_depth/parent_hashes/parent_tool_ids threading, but the public run_chain MCP response trims `artifact` from each step summary and the composite output_payload.steps (§21.2) carries no per-RAN-step chain_depth/parent_* triple. §21 does not state whether §21.1 threading must be independently verifiable through the public surface. This floor verifies it via the one observable §21 does expose end-to-end: the composite artifact's own chain.parent_hashes/parent_tool_ids.

SPEC.md §21.4 does not state what happens when a rule's `next` targets a non-existent step id. run_chain's own code defensively clamps an unresolvable/backward target to idx+1 (worker.mjs), which is not derivable from §21.4's normative text (§21.4 treats forward-only/valid targets and acyclicity as a static property enforced by validate-chains, §15). This floor names the gap; it does not assert or invent a specific runtime fallback contract.
